requirements.title: Sequential ENDFILE writes a last endfile record and positions after it
requirements.definition: Execution of ENDFILE for a sequential-access file writes an endfile record as the next record; the file is positioned after that endfile record, which becomes the last record.

requirements.title: Direct-access reconnection after sequential ENDFILE reads only records before the endfile record
requirements.definition: If a sequential file can also be connected for direct access, only records before the endfile record are considered written and only those records shall be read during subsequent direct access connections.

pending.direct-access-after-endfile-only-before-: No portable oracle for the conditional premise that the same external file can also be connected for direct access with matching representation; future tests may guard on a successful direct connection and assert only records before the endfile.
No portable negative oracle requires a processor to diagnose or produce a particular status when attempting to read beyond the endfile-created written set under direct access.

requirements.title: Sequential ENDFILE requires BACKSPACE or REWIND before later transfer or ENDFILE
requirements.definition: After ENDFILE for a sequential-access file, BACKSPACE or REWIND shall be used to reposition before any data transfer input/output statement or ENDFILE statement.

requirements.title: Stream ENDFILE sets the terminal point to the current position and only prior storage units remain written/readable
requirements.definition: Execution of ENDFILE for a stream-access file makes the terminal point equal to the current file position; only file storage units before the current position are considered written and subsequently readable.

requirements.title: Subsequent stream output may write further data after stream ENDFILE
requirements.definition: After ENDFILE for a stream-access file, subsequent stream output statements may be used to write further data to the file.

requirements.title: ENDFILE on a connected nonexistent file creates the file and sequential creation precedes the endfile record
requirements.definition: Execution of ENDFILE for a file that is connected but does not exist creates the file; if sequential, creation occurs prior to writing the endfile record.

accounting.rationale: Sequential endfile effects and conditional later direct-access consequences are split.
Sequential ENDFILE writes/positions after a last endfile record.
Requires BACKSPACE or REWIND after sequential ENDFILE before later transfer or ENDFILE.
Stream terminal-point effects and subsequent stream-output permission are split.
Stream ENDFILE terminal point and readable/written storage-unit effects.
Permits subsequent stream output after stream ENDFILE.
Connected-nonexistent creation and sequential creation-before-marker effects are split.
ENDFILE creates a connected nonexistent file.
Sequential creation occurs before writing the endfile record.
NOTE gives an ENDFILE example; not normative.
